answer: Require each agent to post a costly bond before it can earn reputation, then slash that bond when independently verified counterparties report fraud. A newcomer can forge names cheaply, but cannot cheaply forge the history of trusted, repeated exchanges: splitting activity across Sybils dilutes each identity’s track record. To attack at scale, the adversary must lock up capital in every account and risk losing it; the resulting cost sends a ripple through the network, while honest agents gain a velvet-smooth path to trust through consistent behavior.
